policy: Correct and fail-closed on generated outdoor-unit support, service-line and drain interfaces before realtime reflection or native-4K evidence. This is source/scene construction QA only and awards zero Visual Fidelity points without actual rendered evidence.
manufactureModel: Each generated balcony condenser is a separate sheet-metal/plastic outdoor unit with a front fan/grille, a bottom chassis supported at two manufactured feet, and discrete service/drain connections rather than a box fused into the balcony slab.

The outdoor unit is mechanically supported above the slab by two visible feet/pads on thin mounting plates; support hardware must remain outside the concrete walking surface and must carry the chassis rather than float below it.

Paired insulated refrigerant lines leave the unit side, turn toward the facade and enter through a sleeved/collared wall penetration. Their elbows and joints must meet geometrically rather than being approximated by disconnected cylinders.
A condensate drain hose leaves low on the unit and terminates just above the balcony surface so water can discharge without the hose visibly penetrating the slab.
Wall clips and the penetration collar are facade-mounted service hardware; moving the condenser vertically must not drag those fixed wall interfaces away from the wall.
installationSequence: Resolve the actual persisted BalconyFloor renderer top for each generated AC bay and verify it remains at the locked fallback elevation.
Seat each mounting plate on the slab top, then seat its vibration/support foot on the plate; neither support component may be hidden inside the concrete.
Raise the condenser chassis only as much as required for its lower face to overlap the top of both support feet by the controlled chassis/foot embed range.

Translate fan disc, hub and grille with the chassis, then reconstruct both insulated refrigerant-line segments from the moved unit-side outlet to the fixed wall-side collar so segment joints stay continuous.
Reconstruct the drain hose from the moved low-side unit outlet to a terminal point 5-20 mm above the balcony surface; retain the wall collar and pipe clips as fixed facade interfaces.
Validate support contacts, lateral support under the chassis, visible bolt heads, pipe continuity and drain clearance before reflection probes or benchmark Camera.Render are allowed.
interfacesGapsSeals: mount-plate bottom to balcony slab top: flush within supportContactTolerance
support-foot bottom to mount-plate top: flush within supportContactTolerance
condenser lower face to foot top: controlled 2-10 mm mechanical visual overlap, target 6 mm
mounting plate and support foot centerlines must remain laterally inside the condenser chassis footprint
refrigerant horizontal/vertical segment joint: endpoint separation <= pipeJointTolerance
drain-hose terminal to slab top: 5-20 mm positive clearance, target 10 mm
visible mount-bolt head must remain above the plate top while retaining a small controlled plate embed

materialsFinish.casing: aged warm off-white coated/plastic exterior; dielectric, low metallic response, mild UV chalking and dirt concentration around grille/recesses rather than painted illumination
materialsFinish.fanAndGrille: dark protected metal/plastic components; physically separate geometry so occlusion and highlights follow the grille depth
materialsFinish.mountingHardware: aged galvanized/protected steel plate and fastener hardware with restrained metallic/specular response and localized contact oxidation only where exposure supports it
materialsFinish.pipeInsulation: aged closed-cell insulation/tape wrap; dielectric, matte, low-frequency compression/UV variation with no metallic highlight
materialsFinish.drainHose: aged flexible polymer; dielectric and relatively matte, with bending represented by geometry rather than a painted stripe
materialsFinish.wallCollar: weathered pipe sleeve/collar at the facade penetration; sheltered/recessed grime can accumulate at the interface

agedAcPlastic.microstructure: fine moulded/coated skin plus localized grille/recess dust
agedAcPlastic.wetness: normally dry; rain spotting only on exposed upper/lateral faces
agedAcPlastic.uvAging: mild warm/chalked shift on sun-facing surfaces
agedAcPlastic.angularFresnel: broad dielectric edge response only; no painted hot edge

galvanizedHardware.microstructure: subtle zinc mottling and contact wear, no large repeated flakes
galvanizedHardware.wetness: localized darkening/roughness change at rain-wet horizontal faces
galvanizedHardware.uvAging: minimal hue shift; oxidation mainly alters roughness/value
galvanizedHardware.angularFresnel: narrower grazing response than casing but dulled by oxidation

pipeInsulation.microstructure: fine tape/foam compression and seam variation
pipeInsulation.wetness: small rain-darkened patches only where exposed
pipeInsulation.angularFresnel: very broad weak dielectric grazing response

drainHose.microstructure: small flexible-hose ribbing where visible at 100% crop
drainHose.wetness: possible darker terminal region from condensate

orientationExposureAging: condenser front and upper surfaces receive midsummer sun/rain; recesses behind grille stay darker through geometry/occlusion, not baked albedo
support plates/feet sit in a contact/splash zone and may show grime or oxidation concentrated near slab contact and fasteners
refrigerant insulation is partly sheltered near the wall but more UV/rain exposed near the unit; aging should follow that gradient
drain outlet is low and can create localized ordinary condensate wetting/residue immediately below/near the outlet, never arbitrary streaks
geometryVsMaterialDetail: casing height, feet, mounting plates, fastener heads, fan/grille depth, pipes, elbows, clips, collar and drain clearance are geometry/interface facts
plastic chalking, galvanized dulling, insulation wrap texture, grime, micro-scratches and localized wetness are material/microdetail
contact shadows, pipe occlusion and grazing highlights must arise from physical geometry plus coherent midsummer lighting, never from albedo highlights
lodPolicy: LOD0 retains fan disc/hub, crossed grille members, two feet/plates, visible fastener heads, paired refrigerant lines, drain hose, collar and clips for native 4K balcony-service crops.
LOD1 may simplify grille density and small fasteners while retaining chassis/support silhouette and paired service lines.
LOD2 merges grille microgeometry and line clips while preserving unit silhouette, mounting gap and service-line bend silhouette.
LOD3 may reduce to a compact authored silhouette/material set but must not collapse into an exposed Unity primitive in benchmark framing; transition stability remains separately reviewed.

lookdevBrief.frontal: Native 3840x2160 facade view: unit must read as a supported manufactured appliance, not a floating box or slab-embedded prop; verify warm aged casing against darker grille and physically separate support gap.
lookdevBrief.oblique: Balcony-services 100% crop: verify both support stacks, chassis-to-foot contact, pipe bends/joints, wall collar and drain terminal clearance with coherent contact shadow.
lookdevBrief.grazing: Midsummer grazing-light crop: casing remains broad dielectric, galvanized mounting hardware responds more sharply, and pipe insulation/drain hose remain matte without baked edge highlights.
lookdevBrief.macro100Percent: Reject buried plates/feet/bolts, floating chassis, disconnected pipe cylinders, drain/slab penetration, z-fighting, light leaks or inconsistent metallic response.
